items.title: Justin Sun seeks $264K sanctions over World Liberty’s UAE disclosure
items.summary: Sun plans to refile his token-freeze lawsuit in California state court after the sanctions motion is resolved. A hearing is set for Dec. 10.

items.title: Bitcoin price threatens $77.7K support loss with recent buyers underwater
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below the realized price of the one-to-three-month-old buyer cohort in a move that risked flipping it to new resistance.

items.title: The election changes Washington. The work on crypto continues
items.summary: The next Congress inherits an unfinished assignment: establishing clear, lasting rules for digital assets that protect consumers and ensure American innovation continues to thrive, writes Blockchain Association's Lindsay Fraser.

items.title: Live updates: Bitcoin and stocks post big gains, reversing overnight plunge following Blue Wave landslide
items.summary: The biggest losers, so far, are the AI data center stocks following victories for several candidates who campaigned expressly against the sector.

items.title: Global asset manager Schroders brings emerging market bond fund to Solana
items.summary: The global asset manager, which oversees $1.1 trillion in assets, is bringing an actively managed bond strategy onchain through tokenization specialist Centrifuge.

items.title: THORChain's RUNE jumps 10% as North Korean hackers resume laundering Binance loot
items.summary: North Korea’s TraderTraitor is routing Binance hack proceeds through THORChain, swapping ether for bitcoin after an earlier wave of conversions from Tron.

items.title: Circle beats earnings expectations on strong revenue, but cuts 5% of its workforce
items.summary: Circle’s net income for continuing operations of $226 million grew 5% year-over-year to $226 million in the third quarter.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds from midterm dip as DeFi leads gains
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered from a dip to around $75,600 as Democrats won Congress, while DeFi tokens led gains and Trump-linked coins fell.

items.title: ZachXBT names French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa as suspected victim of $133 million crypto theft
items.summary: Blockchain sleuth ZachXBT says the French bank may have lost more than $133 million from crypto exchange accounts. Crypto.com confirms it has blocked funds linked to the theft.

items.title: Elon Musk floats space data centers as Democratic sweep puts pressure on AI trade
items.summary: Texas election result raises fears of data centre restrictions, while Musk and Palihapitiya draw attention to the space economy.

items.title: Morgan Stanley says it is among the first banks to tokenize real world assets
items.summary: The bank's announcement follows the launch of the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation’s Tokenization Service, or DTS, on Oct. 28.

items.title: Zcash grants committee drops plan to redirect 98,000 ZEC to future mining rewards
items.summary: The committee withdrew its proposal after community backlash, leaving competing plans to cut off its funding or preserve the existing grants system.

items.title: Bitcoin rises to $78,300 in V-shaped comeback as midterm election uncertainty fades
items.summary: Crypto prices reversed overnight losses following the Blue Wave landslide for the Democratic Party.

items.title: Jack Dorsey's Block faces $764 million DOJ settlement as bitcoin profit plunges 50%
items.summary: The proposed agreement would resolve a federal anti-money-laundering investigation, while lower Cash App trading fees halved Block's quarterly bitcoin gross profit.

items.title: U.S.-sanctioned Moscow Exchange to list bitcoin and Tether’s USDT in December
items.summary: Russia’s main bourse wants back the crypto trading Russians do abroad, and one of the coins it's listing is issued by a company that freezes wallets on the U.S. sanctions list.

items.title: South Korea's ruling party wants to delay its crypto tax again
items.summary: South Korea's ruling party wants to delay crypto tax by about two years, as it waits for global tax-sharing rules and new digital assets law.

items.title: Democrats surge toward Senate, House majorities, with crypto braced for new direction
items.summary: The dominance of Republicans in all three government branches has been broken by the midterms, and the industry will feel the result as Congress changes hands.
